title: Probing the initial geometry and the onset of collectivity with anisotropic flow in light-ion collisions with ALICE at the LHC
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP2026)
summary:
Collective behavior, traditionally associated with heavy-ion collisions, has been observed in small collision systems at the LHC. The recent oxygen-oxygen and neon-neon collisions allow to bridge the gap between small and large collision systems and to study the collectivity in well-constrained initial states. Measurements of azimuthal anisotropies are sensitive to the initial-state geometry and enable detailed investigations of the nuclear structure of $^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne, highlighting the interplay between nuclear structure and collective dynamics in ultrarelativistic collisions.
  This contribution presents recent anisotropic flow measurements performed by the ALICE Collaboration in OO and Ne-Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}$ = 5.36 TeV using two- and multiparticle correlation methods. The results are compared to hydrodynamic calculations incorporating the possible nuclear structures of these light nuclei, providing stringent constraints on the modeling of the initial state. In addition, prospects for measuring long-range correlations with the forward ALICE detectors are discussed, with the aim of studying the longitudinal dependence of anisotropic flow and thereby constraining the longitudinal structure of the initial state.

title: Possible Solution to the Gallium Anomaly? Nuclear Transition Densities
summary: The gallium anomaly, a 20% deficit in the measured $ν_e$ captures on $^{71}$Ga, remains unexplained. A recent work [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131805 (2026), arXiv:2512.20560] has proposed a solution based on the breakdown of the factorization of lepton and nuclear wavefunctions that underlies the prediction of the cross section, combined with ad hoc Gamow-Teller nuclear transition densities. We test this proposed solution with transition densities calculated within the nuclear shell model (NSM), normalized to the $^{71}$Ge electron-capture half-life and convolved with Dirac-Hartree-Fock-Slater electron wavefunctions. We explore several NSM interactions, bare and effective Gamow-Teller operators, as well as the impact of the valence space. In all cases, we obtain remarkably consistent NSM transition densities. Our factorized and nonfactorized cross sections agree, remaining 20% higher than the measured value. In addition, we use NSM single-nucleon transition densities as ansatz and find that solving the anomaly requires fine-tuned densities, with percent-level cancellations and an overall scale orders of magnitude larger than the calculated NSM ones. We conclude that the gallium anomaly is not solved when using realistic nuclear transition densities.

title: Features of Non-Local Quantum Correlations in Nuclei
summary: Classical simulation of quantum many-body systems is challenged by the combined effects of entanglement and non-stabilizerness (magic). Non-local magic, $M^{\mathrm{NL}}_α$, quantifies the component of non-stabilizerness that cannot be removed by local unitary transformations and provides a measure of quantum complexity beyond entanglement alone. It is bounded from below by the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum, ${F}_A$. We calculate stabilizer Rényi entropies, non-local magic, entanglement-spectrum antiflatness, and entanglement entropy in shell-model ground states of more than 260 even-even, odd-even, and odd-odd nuclei, using a bipartition into proton and neutron sectors. We find that the previously established bound $4{F}_A\leq{M}^{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathrm{lin}}$ holds for every nucleus studied and approaches saturation in the limit of separable states. Odd-odd nuclei exhibit markedly different patterns of entanglement and magic compared with even-even and odd-even systems, revealing distinctive signatures of proton-neutron quantum correlations and providing new insight into the complexity generated by nuclear interactions.

title: Baryon Number Susceptibilities of Hot and Dense Nuclear Matter in Relativistic Mean-Field Models
summary: We develop a fully analytical framework for calculating baryon number susceptibilities in relativistic mean-field (RMF) models of hot and dense nuclear matter at finite temperature and baryon chemical potential. The formalism is applied to representative nonlinear RMF parameterization sets to investigate the model dependence of baryon number fluctuations over a wide range of temperatures and baryon chemical potentials. All the considered RMF parameterizations reproduce the overall qualitative beam-energy dependence of the cumulant ratios. The observed skewness and kurtosis within the RMF models satisfy the experimental values. Specifically, the FSU-family parameterizations exhibit relatively small deviations from the measured heavy-ion observables i.e. cumulant ratios.

title: Flat "Island of Stability" of Superheavy Nuclei
summary: We present the first systematic microscopic calculations of fission barrier heights for 292 even-even superheavy nuclei using the multidimensionally constrained relativistic mean field model with triaxial and octupole deformations treated simultaneously. The calculated barrier heights remain around 5 MeV in the vicinity of the predicted doubly magic nucleus ${}^{304}120$. This flat landscape contrasts with the conventional picture of mutually enhanced magicity and indicates that the proton shell closure at $Z=120$ and the neutron shell closure at $N=184$ do not reinforce but suppress each other. We introduce an $α$-linked energy difference $Δ_{\rm pn}$ to identify the mutually suppressed magicity caused by distinct proton and neutron density distributions. These results challenge the expected shell landscape of superheavy nuclei and may have a crucial impact on estimating survival probabilities in the synthesis of superheavy nuclei.

title: Quasi-hydrodynamics beyond the conventional paradigm
summary: Quasi-hydrodynamics extends hydrodynamics by promoting slowly relaxing variables to additional degrees of freedom. For such a framework to be rigorously defined and parametrically controlled, the effective theory is usually assumed to retain all the slow modes of the underlying microscopic dynamics, which must be parametrically separated from the rest of the microscopic spectrum and typically arise from weakly broken symmetries. Here, we show that none of these assumptions is essential. Using the effective field theory of quasi-hydrodynamics recently derived from kinetic theory, we study three models that challenge the need for, respectively, parametric scale separation, retaining every slow mode, and a weakly broken symmetry. In all cases, the quasi-hydrodynamic expansion remains fully controlled and can be made arbitrarily accurate. This is possible because the applicability of quasi-hydrodynamics is determined not by the microscopic origin of the slow dynamics, but by the spectral properties of the kinetic operator on a suitably chosen Hilbert space.

title: Effect of collective nuclear vibrations on initial anisotropies in central Pb+Pb collisions: A comparative study in Glauber and Trento models
summary: We perform a comparison of the Glauber and Trento model predictions for the initial state azimuthal anisotropies $ε_{2,3}\{2\}$ in central Pb+Pb collisions at the LHC energies. We incorporate the quantum collective effects in $^{208}$Pb by sampling nucleon positions with filterings in the quadrupole and octupole moments. We use the data-driven filters adjusted to reproduce the mean squared quadrupole and octupole moments extracted from the experimental strength functions. We find that the collective effects reduce considerably the $ε_2\{2\}/ε_3\{2\}$ ratio. The reduction is more pronounced in the Trento model. We obtain $ε_2\{2\}/ε_3\{2\}\approx 0.75÷0.79(0.68÷0.71)$ in the Glauber(Trento) models. These values allow to resolve the $v_2$-to-$v_3$ puzzle.

title: Mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of BDNK hydrodynamics: from heavy-ion collisions to astrophysics
summary: We present new developments in the mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of the causal and stable first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamic theory by Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha, and Kovtun (BDNK) in general spacetimes. We develop two independent flux-conservative algorithms for arbitrary 3+1-dimensional spacetime metrics. Both are hyperbolic, causal, and well-posed, pass convergence tests, and reproduce known results. The first uses a new first-order reduction with mathematically preserved constraints, whose numerical violations can be handled with cleaning fields (the resulting coupled system is proven hyperbolic and well-posed). The second uses a new mixed-order formulation, whose solutions are proven strictly equivalent to the original BDNK system, without cleaning fields. Our proofs rely on a new general theorem providing sufficient conditions for transforming a mixed-order system with arbitrary-order equations into a strictly hyperbolic system, strengthening a classical result by Choquet Bruhat for weak hyperbolicity. We introduce a new practical prescription for selecting admissible hydrodynamic frames for a broad class of equations of state, including nonconformal ones relevant to heavy-ion collisions and astrophysics. Our simulations capture viscous shock broadening and suppression of Kelvin--Helmholtz vortices, reproduce Bjorken and Gubser flows, and study departures from stationary ideal-fluid configurations in Michel accretion and rotating tori on fixed Schwarzschild and Kerr backgrounds. For heavy-ion collisions, we perform boost invariant simulations with a lattice-QCD-based equation of state and fluctuating TRENTo initial conditions, comparing BDNK with a minimal Israel--Stewart theory. The descriptions agree at small shear viscosity but can differ substantially at larger viscosities, particularly for early initialization with rapid longitudinal expansion.

title: On the collective flow puzzle in ultra-central heavy-ion collisions
summary: Using UCC-DiffHIC, an AI-accelerated event-by-event hydrodynamic model validated against hybrid simula- tions, we study flow in ultracentral Pb-Pb collisions. For suitable initial conditions, the calculated v2{2}/v3{2} approaches unity in the most central collisions, consistent with experiment. An exact response decomposition shows that residual fluctuations suppress the ratio through P3/P2 < 1, where P2 and P3 are Pearson response correlations for elliptic and triangular flow, respectively. This resolves the apparent flow hierarchy without requiring a breakdown of linear response or additional effects such as nuclear deformation.

title: New Neutron Polarizabilities from Deuterium Compton Scattering at HI$γ$S
summary: Elastic and inelastic Compton-scattering cross sections of the deuteron were measured at HI$γ$S using a circularly polarized, quasi-monoenergetic $γ$-ray beam (61.0 MeV). Scattered $γ$ rays from a liquid deuterium target were detected at $55^\circ$, $115^\circ$, and $150^\circ$. High-resolution NaI(Tl) detectors at backward angles enabled separation of elastic and inelastic events. A $χ$EFT analysis of the data yields new neutron scalar polarizabilities, $α^n_{E1} = 12.25 \pm 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \pm 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \pm 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ and $β^n_{M1} = 2.95 \mp 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \mp 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \mp 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ (in units of $10^{-4} \mathrm{fm}^3$) reducing statistical uncertainties by 12 %.
